motions.motion_text: Court Member Never moved, seconded by Court Member. Motion to approve House Agenda Items 8A thru 3C. Bill Item 34 amended.

Council Member Jones moved, seconded by Council Member Karakohian to approve Resolution Nos. 267, 268 and 269 relating to the adoption of the CACD Initiative for 2015.
Council Member Weaver moved, seconded by Council Member Young to approve Resolution Nos. 192, 193 and 194 relating to the adoption of the UACID budget for 2015.
Council Member Young moved, seconded by Council Member Press to approve Resolution No. 138 relating to the adoption of the Boulder Municipal Property Authority budget for 2015.

Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Council Member Jones to approve Resolution Nos. 46, 47 and 48 relating to the adoption of the Boulder Forest Glen Transit Pass General Improvement District budget for 2015.

Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Council Member Morzel to approve Resolution Nos. 11, 12 and 13 relating to the adoption of the Boulder Junction Access Commission Parking Fund budget for 2015.

Council Member Shoemaker moved, seconded by Council Member Weaver to approve Resolution Nos. 11, 12 and 13 relating to the adoption of the Boulder Junction Access District Travel Demand Management budget for 2015.

Council Member Plass moved, seconded by Council Member Morze, to adopt the memorandum and its findings and to deny the application for the demolition of the contributing accessory building finding that it would have a damaging effect on the property within the Mapleton Hill Historic District per Section 9-11-18(b)(1)(A) BRC 98. Approves with conditions an Alteration certificate for the construction of a rear deck, porch, and fence. Finding the proposal meets the standards for the issuance of a Landmark Alteration Certificate in Section 2-1-3.4.R.C. and Conditions of Approval 1. The applicant shall: a. Reconstruct the demolished accessory building in its original location based upon photographic evidence; b. Remove a sufficient amount of the current hardscape such that no more than 50% of the hardscape as defined as the area between the back plane of the home and the front of the alley is covered by hardscape; c. Remove the fire pit, retaining walls and plan for retaining walls; d. Revise fence design to a maximum height of 7'0"; • Submission/Review by Design Review Committee materials, color and pattern mapping. 2. The applicant shall submit the details for the work as described above. These design details shall be reviewed (and approved) by the Landmarks Design Review Committee prior to the issuance of a building permit. The applicant shall demonstrate that the design details are in compliance with the intent of this approval and the Mapleton Hill Historic District Design Guidelines and the General Design Guidelines . 3. The applicant shall be responsible for completing the work as shown on plans that have been approved.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 8-0, with Council Member Karikerian recused.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Morzel offered a friendly amendment, which was accepted by Council Member Glass, to require all work to be completed by a date approved by staff.
Council Member Weaver offered a friendly amendment, which was accepted by Council. Members Plass and Morzel, to allow the fence height up to a maximum height of 5'6".
Council Member Young offered a friendly amendment to require the deck be reduced to the original 88 square feet approved.
He offered a friendly amendment that required the concrete be replaced with pavers and sand so the surface would no longer be impervious.
Mayor Apselbaum moved, seconded by Council Member Morzel, to suspend the rules and continue the meeting.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 3-0, with Council Member Karakshian absent.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Shoemaker moved, seconded by Mayor Appelbaum, to direct the City Manager to negotiate a contract for June 2015 in 2015 and 2016.
Mayor Appellaum moved, seconded by Council Member Cowles, to appoint a 2 member sub-committee to conduct a peer review of compensation to the 3 Council employees.
Mayor Appellaum moved, seconded by Council Member Karakahan, to ratify the Board and Commission appointments.

Council Member Morzel moved, seconded by Council Member Plass, to support Council Member Morzel's request to propose a motion to the Rocky Plains Stewardship Council requesting the Department of Fish and Wildlife to hold the proposed controlled hunt.

Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Council Member Morzel, to authorize the City Manager to sign a Memorandum of Understanding and legal sponsorship agreement formalizing the existence of a regional group known as "Making Local Foods Work."
There being no further business to come before Council at this time, BY MOTION REGULARLY ADOPTED, THE MEETING WAS ADJOURNED on October 21, 2014 at 1:59 PM.

motions.motion_text: Mayor Appelbaum moved, seconded by Council Member Morze, to approve the agenda as amended.
Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Council Member Morzel, to approve Consent Agenda Item 3A through 3C.

Council Member Jones moved, seconded by Council Member Weaver, to adopt Ordinance No. 790 submitting to the registered electors of the City of Bowling Green at the special municipal coordinated election to be held on Tuesday, November 4, 2014, the question of affirming the city's right to provide high-speed internet services (advanced services), telecommunications services, and/or cable television services to residents, businesses, schools, libraries, non-profit entities and other users of such services and setting forth related details.
Mayor Appelhorn moved, seconded by Council Member Weaver, to continue this item until the regular meeting on August 19, 2014.

Council Member Plass moved, seconded by Council Member Shoemaker, to adopt Ordinance No. 7982 submitting to the registered elections of the City of Boulder a the Special Coordinated Municipal Election to be held on Tuesday, November 4, 2014, the question of amending City Charter Section 9 to provide that the city council may meet in executive session only for the purpose of discussing legal advice and negotiation strategy relating to the creation of a municipal electric utility with such authority ending December 31, 2017, setting forth the ballot title and specifying the form of the ballot and all ancillary items.
Mayor Applebaum offered a friendly amendment, accepted by both the maker and seconder of the motion, to include that the amendment at the end of (o).

Council Member Karakenian moved seconded by Council Member Shoemaker to approve Ordinance No. 7983 as amended by the minor corrections presented by the City Attorney on the peach colored handout and by amending the short title of the ballot issue to read "temporary tax increase for Community Culture and Safety."

Council Member Murra moved, seconded by Council Member Weaver, to adopt Resolution No. 1136 and Resolution No. 1137, finding the properties located at 4270 19 th St and 2130 Tamarack Ave. to be unlivable, finding compliance with statutory requirements applicable to these annexations and establishing August 3, 2014 is the date for Council action and to adopt Emergency Ordinance No. 7984 and Emergency Ordinance No. 7985 amending the properties with a final zoning classification of Residential - Estate4 (RB).
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 7-1 with Councilman absent at 9:47 PM.

motions.motion_text: Mayor Appelbaum moved, seconded by Council Member Wertz, to suspend the rules and continue the meeting.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 34, with Council Member Morzel opposed.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Weaver moved, seconded by Council Member Jones, to accept the 2017 Transportation Master Plan and to accept the revised Transportation Master Plan Summary for inclusion in the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan.
Mayor Appelbaum moved, seconded by Council Member Pass, to ratify the Board and Commission appointments.
There being no further business to come before Council at this time, BY MOTION REGULARLY ADOPTED, THE MEETING WAS ADJOURNED on August 6, 2014 at 12:00 AM.

motions.motion_text: Mayor Appelbaum moved, seconded by Council Member Morzel, to approve Ordinance No. 7920 submitting to the registered electors of the City of Boulder in the general municipal coordinated election to be held on Tuesday, November 5, 2013, an alternative ballot question amending the City Charter to address issues presented by the proposed limited Charter amendment that adds a new section .88 on limitations on receipt and use of debt as presented in addition to with the debt limit as indicated at $217,000,000.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 8-0 with Council Member Wilson absent.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Mayor Appelbaum, to take up agenda item 8B while staff worked on incorporating the amendments to Ordinance No. 7920.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried. Abs. Council Member Wilson absent. at 12:31 a.m.

motions.motion_text: Mayor Appelbaum moved, seconded by Council Member Axton to ratify the Board Appointments to the Board of Zoning Adjustments (BOZA) and the Environmental Advisory Board.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 8/0 with Council Member Wilson absent. at 1:20 am.

motions.motion_text: There being no further business to come before Council at this time, BY MOTION REGULARLY ADOPTED, THE MEETING WAS ADJOURNED on August 7, 2013 at 1:20 AM.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Gray moved, seconded by Osborne to authorize the city manager to enter into (a) a development agreement and lease for the city-owned Historic Depot substantially consistent with the provisions set forth in Attachment A, and (b) the conveyance of property into the proposed condominium association at Depot Square including terms implementing the provisions and guiding principles set forth in Attachment B, related to the 8.1 acre city-owned site in Boulder Junction known as the “Boulder Transit Village.”

Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Morzel to approve the Open Space Board recommendations 1 (a) and (b). 2 and 3 with option 4 no longer considered - to read as follows: 1. Emphasize the importance of the overarching issue of “connecting” local OSMP lands with more distant OSMP and County Open Space lands for the benefit of all users in order to increase access and safety including: a. Further consideration of extending the Boulder Creek Path to the current Betasso trail-head in Boulder Canyon. b. Further consideration of an alternative connection to Betasso from the intersection of Boulder and Fourmile Canyons 2. Oppose a connector to Fourmile Canyon due to environmental, neighborhood and safety impacts. 3. Oppose a connection from the Dome area due to the environmental impacts and limited practical use. 4. Look broadly at connection opportunities and focus on cooperation with United States Forest Service, the State of Colorado, Boulder County and private landowners. 5. Not construct switchbacks on the north side of Anemone Hill connecting the Sunshine Canyon trail to the ridge loop.
Council Member Appelbaum offered an amendment to the motion, seconded by Gray to take the switchbacks that connect Sunshine Canyon trail to the Ridge Loop be taken off the plan.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 7:2; Becker and Wilson opposed.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Karakehian moved, seconded by Morzel to approve the consent agenda items 3A through 3C, items 3E and F, items H through K and items M and N.

Council Member Gray moved, seconded by Karakehian to support the staff recommended option for addressing trash and food waste attractants to black bears through building community awareness and utilizing an adaptive management approach based on program success (Option One); and support the staff recommended approach to improving mountain lion awareness and communication.

Council Member Morzel moved, seconded by Karakehian to continue with an enhanced nuisance mosquito control program that 1) targets mosquito control treatments, including more emphasis on irrigation practices and mechanical control of vegetation, to reduce complaints 2) Considers the environmental impacts of treatment decisions 3) Continues the partnership with Boulder County to reduce insecticide applications for adult mosquitoes on adjacent county properties 4) if more than 150 mosquitoes are counted in one week, all 35 breeding sites that Ottertail has identified are to be treated and 5) one citizen representative should be included on the working group.

Council Member Morzel moved, seconded by Karakehian to direct staff to continue with an enhanced nuisance mosquito control program that 1) targets mosquito control treatments, including more emphasis on irrigation practices and mechanical control of vegetation, to reduce complaints 2) Considers the environmental impacts of treatment decisions 3) Continues the partnership with Boulder County to reduce insecticide applications for adult mosquitoes on adjacent county properties.

Council Member Morzel moved, seconded by Appelbaum to reschedule the April 19, 2011 Council meeting to Tuesday, April 12, 2011.
Council Member Morzel moved, seconded by Appelbaum authorize the city manager to enter into an agreement with the Colorado Department of Transportation (CDOT) to accept grant No. 11-BDU-01.
Council Member Appelbaum moved, seconded by Ageton to accept the work program outline and stakeholder structure and process to develop a Capital Investment Strategy.

public_hearings.description: The motion carried unanimously 9:0.

motions.motion_text: Deputy Mayor Wilson moved, seconded by Morzel to approve consent items 3A through 3H with amendments to items 3A and 3D.

Council Member Gray moved, seconded by Morzel to adopt Ordinance No. 7716 amending Title 6 by the addition of a new chapter 6-14, "Medical Marijuana," B.R.C. 1981; terminating interim regulations adopted by Ordinance No. 7707; adding a new section 4-20-64, "Medical Marijuana Dispensaries," to Chapter 4-20, "Fees," B.R.C.1981; amending Title 5 by adding crimes related to anti-personnel devices; and setting forth related details. The motion included the errata sheet amending page 37, line 17 – page 38, line 2 to substitute the following: Section 2. Chapter 4-20 "Fees," B.R.C. 1981 is amended by the addition of a new section 4-2064, to read: 4-20-64 Medical Marijuana Businesses. Application and license fees for medical marijuana businesses shall be up to the following amounts: (a) Application fee | $3,000.00 (b) Criminal background check fee, per year | Actual Costs (c) License fee, per year | $23,000.00 (d) Renewal application fee, per year | $21,000.00 (e) Renewal license fee, per year | $1,000.00 The actual amount of the application and license fees shall be set by the City Manager up to the maximums provided above based on the anticipated direct and indirect costs to the City of preparing to issue licenses, processing applications, and monitoring compliance of medical marijuana business. The application fee and costs paid are non-refundable. The license fee may be refunded if the license application is denied. Neither the application fee nor the license/renewal fee will be refunded in the instance of revocation.

Council Member Becker moved, seconded by Wilson to remove the underline on page 30, lines 15-17. The following sentence in section (f) deleted: “Provided however, deliver of medical marijuana from the licensed premises to a patient may be permitted in the event a patient has an emergency need for medical marijuana prior to 7 a.m. of the following day. In such case, the delivery shall be no more medical marijuana than is required to meet the need of the patient to address the emergency.”

Council Member Ageton moved, seconded by Cowles to delete Sections 3 and 4 of the ordinance on page 38 of the memo and introduce and order published by title only a new Ordinance No. 7723 as presented in the green supplemental handout provided by the City Attorney, amending Title 5 “General Offenses,” B.R.C. 1981 by adding crimes related to anti-personnel devices, and setting forth related details.

Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Becker to amend section (i) by deleting “or Offset” in the subject and removing “...Certified Renewable Energy Credits (“RECs”) or carbon offsets. For purposes of this section RECs or offsets means independently certified carbon credits established through programs such as Green E. The new section (i) now reads: Renewable Energy Usage Required. Every medical marijuana business that grows medical marijuana on premise shall directly offset 100% of its electricity consumption through the purchase of renewable energy in the form of Windsource, a verified subscription in a Community Solar Garden or renewable energy generated on site, or an equivalent that is subject to approval by the city.
Council Member Appelbaum offered a friendly amendment to eliminate Green E and the Colorado Carbon Fund on line 26 of page 30.
Council Member Gray offered a friendly amendment to amend line 26 to read “...Community Solar Garden or renewable energy generated on site.

Council Member Appelbaum moved, seconded by Morzel to amend Section (a) subsection (2) on page 21 of the memo by deleting “is located as allowed in Ordinance No. 7707” and inserting “was established as a greenhouse/nursery use and prior to “commenced operation..”
Council Member Morzel moved, seconded by Ageton to suspend the rules and continue the meeting at 10:35 p.m.

Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Becker to incorporate the yellow supplemental handout provided by the City Attorney amending page 32, line 18 of “Records of Sources of Medical Marijuana” by adding a new subsection (e) to 6-14-9: 6-14-9 Right of Entry – Records To Be Maintained. (e) Reporting of Source, Quantity and Sales. The records to be maintained by each licensee shall include the source and quantity of any marijuana distributed, produced or possessed upon the licensed premises. Such reports shall include without limitation for both acquisitions from wholesalers and transactions to patients or caregivers the following: 1. Name and address of seller or purchaser; 2. Date, weight, type of marijuana and dollar amount or other consideration of transaction; and 3. For wholesale transactions, the Colorado, and city if any, sales and use tax license number of the seller. And deleting Section 6-14-12(b) on page 34, lines 6-8 as shown on the yellow handout provided by the City Attorney.

Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Wilson to incorporate the blue supplemental handout provided by the City Attorney amending page 32, line 18 by adding a new Subsection (e) to 6-14-9: 6-14-9 Right of Entry – Records To Be Maintained. (e) Reporting of Energy Use and Renewable Energy Credit (REC) Purchases. The records to be maintained by each licensee that grows medical marijuana shall include without limitation records showing on a monthly basis the use and source of energy and the number of certified Renewable Energy Credits (RECs) purchased, or the subscription level for another renewable energy acquisition program approved by the city manager. Such records shall include all statements, reports or receipts to verify the items included in the report of the licensee. By acceptance of the medical marijuana business license from the city, the licensee grants permission to providers of the energy or point of origin of the RECs or other renewable energy acquisition program to disclose the records of the licensee to the city.
Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Morzel to amend page 28, line 21 by adding “except that this limitation shall not apply in Industrial Zones.”
Council Member Ageton moved, seconded by Morzel to suspend the rules and continue the meeting at 11:00 p.m.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 7:2; Cowles and Karakehian opposed.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Gray moved, seconded by Morzel to amend page 28, lines 14 and 16 in section (e) subsection (1) inserting “and for personal service uses, within 500’ of a City Parks and Recreation park or center, excluding the Boulder Creek Path, Pearl Street Mall and Flatirons Golf Course.”
motions.vote_text: The motion failed 3:6; Gray, Morzel and Osborne in favor.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Wilson moved, seconded by Becker to strike the last sentence in (e) (1) on page 28 of the memo that reads “This restriction shall not apply to any applicant who applied for a business license for a medical marijuana business prior to November 5, 2009, such license was approved and the business has continuously operated such business since December 1, 2009.
motions.vote_text: The motion failed 4:5; Ageton, Appelbaum, Cowles, Karakehian and Morzel opposed.

motions.motion_text: Mayor Osborne appointed Council Member Becker to the Boulder Urban Renewal Authority Board.
There was a motion to revisit the Crestview East annexation issues related to sidewalks and trees.
motions.vote_text: The motion failed 3:6; Gray, Cowles and Morzel in favor.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Osborne to approve consent items 3A through 3J with item 3H pulled from consent by Deputy Mayor Gray.

motions.vote_text: The motion failed 4:4; Appelbaum, Ageton, Espinoza, and Osborne opposed.

Council Member Morzel moved, seconded by Appelbaum to approve the staff recommended motion on page 2 of the agenda memo as follows: Motion directing staff to move forward on planning for the revitalization of the Uni-Hill Business District as follows: A. Initiate a short-term effort to be completed by June 2009: 1. Refine the draft problem statement, goals and objectives (see page 15 for initial draft) based on Planning Board's December 18, 2008 feedback and City Council's feedback February 3, 2009 to provide direction for the work plan in item 4 below. 2. Continue with the work underway to address use/alcohol issues (scheduled for an April 2009 City Council study session). 3. Make minor changes to the Land Use Code for presentation to Planning Board for recommendation and City Council for action including: • Exempt all below grade space from the Floor Area Ratio (FAR) calculations (currently 50 % of habitable below grade space is calculated in the allowable FAR). • Consider minor changes to the Business Main Street (BMS) zone and the University Hill General Improvement District (UHGID) boundary 4. Prepare a work plan and schedule for a comprehensive revitalization strategy for direction from Planning Board and City Council, that includes those key issues identified by Planning Board, listed on page 3 of this memo. This would require consulting with the New Hill Company and other stakeholders. B. Initiate development of a comprehensive revitalization strategy, process and schedule, as developed in item d-4 above (to be initiated in 2010).
Council Member Ageton offered a friendly amendment to amend the recommendation to state no later than 2010.

public_hearings.name: CONSIDERATION OF A MOTION RECOMMENDING THE VALMONT CITY PARK FINAL CONCEPT PLAN AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF PHASING STRATEGIES MOVE FORWARD TO SITE REVIEW.
public_hearings.description: Council recommended that the concept plan and phasing strategies move forward to site review, with the reduced-parking friendly amendment, 9:0.

public_hearings.name: INTRODUCTION, FIRST READING AND CONSIDERATION OF A MOTION TO ORDER PUBLISHED BY TITLE ONLY SEVEN ORDINANCES THAT RELATE TO POTENTIAL AMENDMENTS TO THE CHARTER OF THE CITY OF BOULDER, COLORADO. INCLUDED ARE PROVISIONS THAT WOULD: (1) RAISE THE COMPENSATION FOR COUNCIL MEMBERS; (2) ALLOW THE CITY COUNCIL TO CONVENE EXECUTIVE SESSIONS; (3) DELETE CURRENT REQUIREMENTS THAT A PETITION SIGNER'S PLACE OF BUSINESS BE PROVIDED; (4) RAISE THE NUMBER OF SIGNATURES REQUIRED FOR NOMINATION PETITIONS; (5) AMEND THE PROCESS BY WHICH HOLDERS OF ELECTIVE OFFICE MAY BE RECALLED; (6) EXTEND THE LONGEST POTENTIAL TERM FOR A LEASE OF CITY PROPERTY; AND (7) ALTER THE QUALIFICATIONS FOR SERVICE ON BOARDS AND COMMISSIONS TO ALLOW SOME NON-ELECTORS TO SERVE.
public_hearings.description: Council introduced and ordered published by title only Ordinances 7599, 7600, 7603, 7604 and 7605, with amendments, and voted not to introduce Ordinances 7601 and 7602.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Morzel to approve consent items 3A through 3F with item 3A amended as indicated by changes submitted via the council Hotline and incorporating the change requested by City Attorney Gordon on item 3D.
Council Member Ageton offered a friendly amendment to accept a modification to item 3B clarifying on second reading, the definition of motor vehicle and whether it encompasses trailers.
Council Member Osborne offered a friendly amendment to item 3A indicating that she was present at the June 3 Council meeting and the minutes should be amended to reflect that she was present.
Council Member Wilson offered a friendly amendment to item 3A noting that on page 6, the third paragraph should state that there are no home games until September.
Deputy Mayor Gray moved, seconded by Morzel to recommend that the Valmont City Park Concept Plan and the development of phasing strategies move forward to site review.

Council Member Cowles offered a friendly amendment to direct Parks and Recreation to work with Planning and Transportation to reduce the demand for parking while providing for the activities set out in the concept plan.
Council Member Appelbaum moved, seconded by Wilson to introduce and order published by title only, Ordinance No. 7599 placing the question of council compensation on the November 4, 2008 ballot.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 6:3; Ageton, Cowles and Morzel opposed.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Ageton moved, seconded by Appelbaum to introduce and order published by title only Ordinance No. 7600 placing the question of allowing council to convene executive sessions on the November 4, 2008 ballot with an amendment on page 12, under Section 9: "Meetings of council," subsection (a), deleting the word "future," prior to the word "purchase."
Council Member Appelbaum offered a friendly amendment to require a two-third vote of the quorum present to convene an executive session.
Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Morzel NOT introduce Ordinance No. 7601 regarding requirements to include places of business on nomination petitions.
Council Member Morzel moved, seconded by Appelbaum to NOT introduce Ordinance No. 7602 regarding increasing the number of signatures required on nomination petitions.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 5:4; Cowles, Espinoza, Gray and Wilson opposed.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Cowles offered a substitute motion, seconded by Wilson to introduce and order published by title only Ordinance No. 7602 to increase the number of signatures required from 25 signatures to 50 signatures.
motions.vote_text: The motion failed 4:5; Ageton, Appelbaum, McGrath, Morzel, and Osborne opposed.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Wilson moved, seconded by Osborne to introduce and order published by title only Ordinance No. 7603 regarding recall provisions.
Deputy Mayor Gray moved, seconded by Ageton to introduce and order published by title only Ordinance No. 7604 regarding long term leases as amended to 40 years.
Council Member Appelbaum moved, seconded by Cowles to amend the motion by striking the 2/3 vote.
motions.vote_text: The motion failed 3:6; Ageton, Appelbaum, and Cowles.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Appelbaum moved, seconded by Espinoza to introduce and order published by title only Ordinance No. 7605 (option 1) regarding service on boards and commissions.

Deputy Mayor Gray offered a substitute motion, seconded by McGrath to introduce and order published by title only Ordinance No. 7605 (option 1) as drafted in attachment G but to only require residency of one year.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 7:2; Ageton and Morzel opposed.

motions.motion_text: City Attorney Gordon indicated that the ordinance language could be amended in attachment G, page 35, section 130, to remove the word "electors" and replace it with the word "members," and at the end add the phrase, "and who have resided in the city of Boulder for at least one year immediately prior to appointment to serve on the commission.
motions.vote_text: This was accepted as a friendly amendment.

motions.motion_text: Deputy Mayor Gray moved, seconded by McGrath to suspend the rules and continue the meeting at 10:55 p.m.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 5:1; Ageton, Appelbaum, and Cowles absent, Espinoza opposed.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Appelbaum moved, seconded by Gray to continue the meeting at 11:10 p.m.
Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Morzel to direct staff to draft an ordinance to rezone the Orchard Grove property to Mobile Home Zone (M-HZ ) at council's next meeting on July 22.
Council Member Cowles offered a friendly amendment to bring a draft ordinance to rezone the Orchard Grove property to Mobile Home Zone (MH-Z) to council's August 5 meeting.
motions.vote_text: The friendly amendment was not accepted.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Appelbaum offered a substitute motion, seconded by Morzel to direct staff to initiate rezoning of the Orchard Grove property to Mobile Home Zone (MH-Z).
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 7:2; Ageton and McGrath opposed.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Espinoza offered a friendly amendment to direct staff to submit this rezoning to the Planning Board on August 7.
Deputy Mayor Gray moved, seconded by Osborne to call-up the site review for 915 Pearl Street.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 7:2; Cowles and Espinoza opposed.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Morzel to express to the Metro Mayors Caucus that the council does not support the resolution regarding ballot issues affecting employers and labor in Colorado.
motions.vote_text: The motion failed 3:6; Ageton, Appelbaum, Espinoza, McGrath, Osborne, and Wilson opposed.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Mock moved, seconded by Morzel, to approve Consent Agenda items 3-A through 3-E.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried: 7-0, Eldridge and Havlick absent.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Morzel moved, seconded by Riggle, to request that Planning Board evaluate the elimination of the Planning Reserve by changing it to a Rural Preserve in addition to the current proposal to change to 159 acres of Planning Reserve to Rural Preserve adopted by Council on September 5, 2000.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried: 5-2, Corson and Lopez opposed, Eldridge and Havlick absent.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Morzel moved, seconded by Mock , to adopt Option No. 3, to defer Land Use Map changes for Area Plans.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried: 4-3, Corson, Lopez and Poinsatte opposed, Eldridge and Havlick absent.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Morzel moved, seconded by Poinsatte, to direct staff to look at the potential for reducing Commercial Land Use Designations in Area 1 (including options for reducing job growth).
motions.vote_text: The motion carried: 6 - 1, Lopez opposed, Eldridge and Havlick.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Mock moved, seconded by Morzel, to adopt Resolution No. 862. encouraging the citizens of the City of Boulder to oppose Amendment No. 21 also known as “Taxcut 2000,” when voting in the November 7, 2000 election.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried: 7-0, Eldridge and Havlick absent.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Corson moved, seconded by Morzel, to support Boulder County Ballot Question 1B authorizing the extension of the County's existing .10% recycling and composting sales and use tax for eight years and for the issuance of up to $80,800,000 in bonds, for the purchase and maintenance of open space.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried: 7-0, Eldridge and Havlick absent.

motions.motion_text: Mayor Toor moved, seconded by Mock, to adopt Ordinance No.7078, adopting Chapter 6-12, B.R.C. 1981, regulating trash haulers and recyclable materials as amended.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried: 7-0, Eldridge and Havlick absent.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Morzel moved, seconded by Riggle, to approve the Greenways Master Plan projects and opportunities.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried: 7-0. Eldridge and Havlick absent.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Mock moved, seconded by Lopez, to introduce and order published by title only Ordinance No.7083, amending Sections 5-6-2 and 5-6-6, B.R.C. 1981, concerning blank cartridges, fireworks, and exempting certain devices for ceremonial or other purposes as amended.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried: 7-0, Eldridge and Havlick absent.

motions.motion_text: There being no further business to come before Council at this time, BY MOTION REGULARLY ADOPTED, THE MEETING WAS ADJOURNED AT 9:45 p.m.

CONSIDERATION OF A MOTION APPROVING: (1) SUCCESSOR INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGREEMENT TO BOULDER VALLEY TDR (TRANSFERABLE DEVELOPMENT RIGHT) COMPREHENSIVE DEVELOPMENT PLAN INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF BOULDER AND BOULDER COUNTY. (2) JOINT PURCHASE BY THE CITY OF BOULDER AND THE COUNTY OF BOULDER OF CONSERVATION EASEMENTS ESTABLISHING FUTURE PERMITTED DEVELOPMENT AND USES ON PORTIONS OF THE PROPERTY REFERRED TO AS “CARIBOU RANCH,” BOULDER COUNTY, COLORADO, WITH CONDITIONS SETTLING DISPUTES BETWEEN THE CITY, THE COUNTY AND THE OWNERS OF THE PROPERTY; (3) THE CITY FUNDING THE ENTIRE PURCHASE, WITH THE COUNTY REIMBURSING ITS SHARE TO THE CITY OVER FIVE YEARS; (4) AN EASEMENT TO JAMES GUERCIO OF 1.25 ACRES OF LAND ADJACENT TO CARIBOU RANCH; (5) THE MODIFICATION OF PREVIOUS AGREEMENTS WITH JAMES GUERCIO WHEREIN PORTIONS OF LAND THAT WERE TO BE DEEDED TO THE COUNTY IN FEE WILL NOW BE PROTECTED BY CONSERVATION EASEMENTS, AND PORTIONS OF LAND THAT WERE PREVIOUSLY PURCHASED AS “BUFFER LAND” WILL NOW BE PART OF THE DEVELOPMENT, BUT PROTECTED BY CONSERVATION EASEMENTS; (6) RECISSION OF UP TO 250 TDRS CONTEMPLATED BY PRIOR AGREEMENTS BETWEEN THE CITY AND THE COUNTY, PLUS (1) CONVEYANCE OF A PERPETUAL CONSERVATION EASEMENT TO THE COUNTY ON THE APPROXIMATELY 160-ACRE PARCEL AT THE SOUTHEAST CORNER OF THE INTERSECTION OF 95 TH STREET AND LOOKOUT ROAD, (2) APPROVAL OF A PROCESS FOR LOCATING TDRS IN AREA III OF THE BOULDER VALLEY WITH CITY COUNCIL APPROVAL, (3) FORBEARANCE OF OPEN SPACE ACQUISITION OF 120 ACRES LOCATED IMMEDIATELY NORTH AND EAST OF LAKE VALLEY SUBDIVISION (OUTSIDE OF THE BOULDER VALLEY COMPREHENSIVE PLAN AREA) AND AGREEMENT THAT THE COUNTY MAY LOCATE UP TO SIXTY TDRS IN THIS 120 ACRE AREA, AND (4) CITY “ASSURANCES” OF ITS CONTINUING INTENTION TO NEGOTIATE FOR AND ACQUIRE LANDS WITHIN AREA III OF THE BOULDER VALLEY AND THE “NORTHERN TIER” DESIGNATED FOR COOPERATIVE CITY/COUNTY OPEN SPACE ACQUISITION. (7) THE TRANSFERENCE OF THREE PROPERTIES AND WATER FROM THE PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT TO THE OPEN SPACE DEPARTMENT WITH COMPENSATION BY OPEN SPACE TO PUBLIC WORKS AND THE GRANTING BY THE CITY TO THE COUNTY OF A CONSERVATION EASEMENT ON ONE OF THE PROPERTIES.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Mock moved, seconded by Morzel, to approve Consent Agenda items 3-A through 3-G as amended to include Emergency Ordinance No. 7066 for Item 3-G (1).

Councilmember Corson moved, seconded by Morzel, to respond to Denver letting them know that due to risks being higher than anticipated, City of Boulder cannot pursue obtaining Currigan Hall at this time but supports preservation of the building and urges their consideration of other proposals. Further, that if no other parties are identified, the City of Boulder may still be interested in the future.

Councilmember Morzel moved, seconded by Corson, to adopt Ordinance No. 7054 to approve an Intergovernmental Agreement with Boulder County, City of Louisville, Town of Superior and the City of Boulder entitled, “US 36 Corridor Comprehensive Development Plan”.
Councilmember Mock moved, seconded by Corson, to approve the 28 th Street CEAP (South Segment) “Hello Boulder” with consideration to be given to suggestions raised by Council.
Councilmember Morzel moved, seconded by Mock, to introduce and order published by title only Ordinance No. 7065 vacating six access easements located within the Devil's Thumb Subdivision.
There being no further business to come before Council at this time, BY MOTION REGULARLY ADOPTED, THE MEETING WAS ADJOURNED AT 9:34 p.m.
